title: GAO: 24 Federal Agencies Unprepared for Emerging Quantum Computing Cyber Threats
source_used: eWeek (12 Oct 2026) report on the GAO report; Homeland Security Today page blocked (403)
key_facts: A Government Accountability Office (GAO) report publicly released 6 Oct 2026 found that none of the 24 Chief Financial Officers Act agencies had fully addressed three key preparation practices for moving to post-quantum cryptography.

The three practices, drawn from Office of Management and Budget (OMB) guidance, are inventorying systems with vulnerable cryptography, estimating the cost of replacing it, and testing quantum-resistant algorithms.
Only one of the 24 agencies fully completed its inventory; 22 left priority systems out, one had no inventory and 19 used no automated discovery tools.
None fully met the funding practice: 21 agencies submitted estimates they said were not fully accurate and three submitted none.
None tested the new algorithms: one agency identified vendor products to test but ran no tests, and 23 addressed neither testing activity.
The audit ran from February 2024 to September 2025; the public report follows a sensitive version issued to agencies that September.
18 agencies reported a lack of cryptography expertise and no plans to fill the gap; GAO rejected the argument that testing was premature.
Of the 23 agencies that received recommendations, 12 agreed and one disagreed with three of its four; civilian agencies must send OMB migration plans by 22 Oct 2026.
quote_evidence: None of the 24 Chief Financial Officers (CFO) Act agencies had fully addressed three key practices for preparing to move to post-quantum cryptography (PQC), according to a Government Accountability Office (GAO) report publicly released Oct. 6.
Only one agency fully completed its inventory work.
Of the 23 agencies that received recommendations, 12 agreed and one disagreed with three of its four.
why_it_matters_hint: Federal systems holding sensitive data are not yet ready for a future quantum attack, shortly before a 22 Oct 2026 planning deadline.
event_date: 6 Oct 2026 (GAO report public); audit ended Sep 2025
